selection_evidence: results/diagnostics/ablation_v8 (dev seeds 1001-1010, benchmarks/ablation_v8.py): unicycle stop-turn-go (first-order unicycle1 stops and turns in place at nodes; straight edges have zero yaw rate) solves 10/10 on both cases for every variant with 100% independent original-model validation; extension range 1.5 m has the least work among {0.35, 1.5, 6.0}. Pure-sphere shell cover yields identical search work (iterations, edges) to the filled cover on all aerial cases and variants. v7 evidence: results/diagnostics/ablation_low_dof_v7 (dev seeds 1001-1010): unicycle disk sampling + reverse chart + lift 1.0 was the only configuration solving 10/10 on both unicycle cases; spatial-only edge sampling leaves search work unchanged and is the authors' validSegmentCount rule; keeping the SST* graph across phases did not help and is not adopted.
unresolved: VAMP-style extension (target position clipped to range, sampled derivatives kept); ranges 1.5 m (aerial) and 6 m (unicycle, i.e. no clipping) reconstructed
Flat velocity sampling bound 0.5 m/s (aerial), 1.0 m/s (unicycle) reconstructed
Unicycle reverse chart (kappa=1 of Eq. 10) and boundary lift speed 1.0 m/s reconstructed; forward chart fails Bugtrap
Unicycle yaw-rate limit 1.5 rad/s enforced exactly; without it the paper's unicycle times are matched but trajectories violate the stated limit (diagnostic round 7)
Goal regions of propagation planners: DynoBench distance weights and goal_epsilon (sst_v0.yaml); order-two aerial goal uses position/velocity terms only
SST* first phase 10000 iterations; unicycle selection/pruning radii 0.5/0.1 reconstructed
Ten-second FLASK budget; failures retained
Corrective campaign: full order-four aerial original-state validation; all variants retain physical continuity and original boundaries.
Filled conservative sphere cover is used; no surface-only occupancy assumption.
This is a corrected reconstruction profile, not recovered author experiment settings.
Reconstructed aerial rest/uniform sampling mixture with probability 0.5; author sampler unavailable.
Reconstructed unicycle heading-aware metric, scaled by published maximum-speed/maximum-yaw-rate ratio; author metric unavailable.
Physical limits, original boundaries and filled sphere-cover geometry are unchanged from v3.
Per-output control bounds remain an optional diagnostic interface; v4 retains scalar pseudo-control bound 2 for controlled attribution.
Indexed candidate queries refine the original double-precision metric and insertion-order ties; author compound-norm metric retains its scan fallback.

Aerial pruning radius reconstructed as one quarter of RMS propagation displacement; author radius, control bounds and propagation horizon are unconfirmed. This corrects a zero-growth initial phase in Quad2D, not the remaining physical-model or performance gaps.
v7: aerial order 2 = paper-protocol reduced order (Sec. V-C1); attitude/body-rate jumps at joins reported
v7: flat velocity of the unicycle sampled in the disk |v|<=1 (paper speed limit) with a 0.01 m/s hole at the chart singularity
v7: spatial-only edge sampling; between-sample dynamic limits established post hoc by the interval validator

Unicycle: the paper does not state its boundary/sampling protocol; v8 uses stop-turn-go (rest nodes, straight BVP edges, in-place turns at |omega| = 1.5 counted in the trajectory duration); the strict single-chart v7 protocol is reported beside it.

Aerial obstacles: pure-sphere shell cover, equivalent for tree planners because every validator step (<= validation_spacing) is shorter than the shell layer; every returned path is re-checked against the original boxes.
v9: stop-turn-go Alg. 4 bypasses between stopped states (propagated nodes are stored at rest); every seed is timed 5 times with identical work and the median is reported (the first run is kept).
